articles.title: India Just Raised Passport Fees by Up to 67%. The New Rates Hit Tomorrow.
articles.excerpt: A standard 36-page passport now costs ₹2,500, up from ₹1,500. Replacing a lost one under Tatkal will set you back ₹8,500. Here's the full breakdown — and what NRIs applying through missions abroad should know.
articles.image_caption: An Indian passport in a leather travel wallet — fees for renewals and fresh applications rise sharply from July 1
articles.nri_angle: NRIs renewing passports or applying for children's passports through Indian missions abroad face higher fees starting July 1, with costs rising by up to 67% for standard applications and even more for lost passport replacements.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Families Sold 50 Tonnes of Gold Last Quarter. It’s the Biggest Sell-Off in Years.
articles.excerpt: Fearing prices could crater to ₹1.2 lakh per 10 grams, households are ditching heirloom jewellery for cold, hard cash — and India’s gold recycling industry is booming.
articles.image_caption: Gold bullion bars. Indian households sold nearly 50 tonnes of old gold in the April-June quarter, a 43% year-on-year surge driven by fears of further price declines.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs holding family gold in India face the same price correction dynamics. The sell-off signals a generational shift from treating gold as untouchable heirloom to tradable financial asset — a conversation many overseas Indians are having with family back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Lifts Emergency Fuel Restrictions Starting July 1 as Oil Prices Collapse
articles.excerpt: The 200-litre diesel cap and ban on commercial buyers at retail pumps are gone. Brent crude has fallen 42% from its April peak, and windfall taxes are being reshuffled.
articles.image_caption: A Hindustan Petroleum fuel pump in India. Emergency restrictions on diesel and petrol sales at retail outlets will be lifted on July 1.
articles.nri_angle: NRI-owned businesses in transport, manufacturing, and agriculture were directly impacted by the fuel restrictions. The episode highlights India’s energy import vulnerability and the speed at which Middle East conflicts ripple into everyday fuel access.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Supreme Court Just Told 250,000 Babies a Year They're Still American. Here's What It Means for H-1B Families.
articles.excerpt: In a 6-3 ruling on the final day of its term, the court struck down Trump's executive order restricting birthright citizenship — a case that had Indian professionals on temporary visas watching closer than anyone.
articles.image_caption: The Supreme Court of the United States in Washington, D.C.
articles.nri_angle: Indian H-1B holders — the largest group of temporary work visa holders in the US — were directly in the crosshairs of Trump's executive order, which would have stripped US citizenship from their American-born children.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He Called India's Jobless Youth 'Cockroaches.' They Built a Party Around It.
articles.excerpt: The Cockroach Janta Party has 22 million followers, a Boston University graduate at the helm, and an icon of Ladakh on hunger strike at its side. India's education minister may not survive the week.
articles.image_caption: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk, who began an indefinite hunger strike at Jantar Mantar on June 28
articles.nri_angle: The NEET exam scandal directly affects NRI families with children in India's education pipeline, and the movement is led by a Boston University graduate who flew back from the US to organise protests.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He Filed 64 Identical Asylum Claims for Indian Clients. ICE Just Made Him the First Attorney It's Ever Fined for It.
articles.excerpt: California-based Vinod Doddamani faces a $255,000 penalty in a first-of-its-kind crackdown on immigration attorneys. For the Indian diaspora, the fallout goes far beyond one case.
articles.image_caption: The ICE headquarters building in Washington, D.C. — the agency issued its first-ever attorney fine in a crackdown on fraudulent asylum claims (Wikimedia Commons / CC BY 3.0)
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals are disproportionately affected by asylum fraud crackdowns, which can tighten scrutiny on all Indian immigration applicants and feed anti-immigrant narratives that shape H-1B and green card policy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Spent 17% More in Two Months but Used Less Than a Tenth of Its Deficit Budget. Here's How.
articles.excerpt: Fresh government data shows India's April-May fiscal deficit at just 9.6% of its full-year target — down sharply from the alarming 21% burn rate a month earlier. The capex push is real, and so are the risks.
articles.image_caption: The Central Secretariat in New Delhi, seat of India's federal government
articles.nri_angle: India's fiscal discipline directly impacts bond yields, rupee stability, and the investment climate that NRIs and diaspora investors are betting on — the record $3B foreign bond inflows in June are downstream of these numbers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple Calls India's Antitrust Case Against It 'Copy-Pasted.' The Regulator Has Heard That Before.
articles.excerpt: In its sharpest filing yet, Apple accuses the CCI of lifting rivals' claims verbatim instead of running its own investigation. Google tried the same argument — and lost.
articles.image_caption: Apple Park, the company's headquarters in Cupertino, California
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin tech professionals at Apple and Google face scrutiny of their employers' practices, while Indian startups like PhonePe and Paytm push for fairer app store rules that could reshape India's digital economy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Rupee Just Posted Its First Quarterly Gain in Over a Year. Here's What It Took.
articles.excerpt: Oil's 42% crash, a record $3 billion bond surge, and a Goldman Sachs upgrade pulled India's currency back from the brink. NRI wallets feel the difference.
articles.image_caption: Indian rupee banknotes — the currency posted its first quarterly gain since early 2025
articles.nri_angle: The rupee's quarterly gain directly affects the purchasing power of remittances sent by 18 million NRIs, while RBI measures offering up to 7.5% on FCNR deposits create the most attractive NRI inflow proposition in years.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Won't Sign the US Trade Deal Until It Gets a Better Rate Than Pakistan. That's Not Happening Anytime Soon.
articles.excerpt: After the Supreme Court struck down Trump's sweeping tariffs, the 18% deal that looked generous in February now looks like a bad bargain. Commerce Minister Goyal says the agreement is frozen until Washington fixes the math.
articles.image_caption: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal at a government event
articles.nri_angle: A stalled India-US trade deal affects professional services provisions, business visa terms, and the broader diplomatic climate that shapes Indian American daily life.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foreign Investors Just Poured a Record $3 Billion Into Indian Bonds in a Single Month. The Tax Break Worked.
articles.excerpt: New Delhi scrapped capital gains and withholding taxes on government securities. In three weeks, foreigners bought almost twice what they had in the previous five months combined. Now Bloomberg is watching.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters tower in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: The rupee's recovery from near-97 to 94.66 affects remittance values, new FCNR schemes offer NRIs near-7% returns, and the bond market opening could eventually extend to retail NRI participation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Japan's First Female PM Arrives in India Tomorrow. She's Bringing a $68 Billion Investment Playbook.
articles.excerpt: Sanae Takaichi's inaugural visit to New Delhi for the 16th India-Japan Annual Summit will test whether two democracies can outpace China in semiconductors, rare earths, and clean energy.
articles.image_caption: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi in her official portrait
articles.nri_angle: The summit targets 500,000 personnel exchanges over five years including 50,000 skilled Indian workers — expanding career pathways for the diaspora in Japan's tech and manufacturing sectors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran Is Offering India Oil at $4 a Barrel Below Market Price. India Isn't Sure It Can Say Yes.
articles.excerpt: With sanctions lifted for 60 days and Hormuz traffic picking up, Tehran is flooding Indian refiners with offers — through middlemen, ministers, and the state oil company. The catch: nobody knows how to pay.
articles.image_caption: A crude oil tanker at sea — vessels like this carry Iranian crude to Asian refineries
articles.nri_angle: Cheaper Iranian oil would strengthen the rupee, lower India's current account deficit, and ease inflation — directly benefiting the 9 million Indians working in Gulf petrodollar economies and NRI remittance corridors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Monsoon Has Delivered 42% Less Rain Than Normal. Farmers Are Running Out of Time.
articles.excerpt: Kharif sowing is down 23%, cotton acreage has cratered 35%, and a Super El Niño is building. Here's what the worst June rainfall in over a decade means for food prices, markets, and the families NRIs send money home to.
articles.image_caption: Indian farmland dependent on monsoon rains — the 2026 season has delivered 42 per cent less rainfall than the seasonal average (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Weak monsoon threatens to spike food prices for families back home, drag rural incomes that remittances supplement, and weigh on Indian equity markets where NRIs hold significant portfolios.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Merged Its Two Biggest Power Lenders Into a $130 Billion Giant. Here's What It Means.
articles.excerpt: PFC and REC approved a merger on Sunday that creates India's largest non-banking financial company, with a loan book bigger than some of the country's banks.
articles.image_caption: REC Limited corporate headquarters in New Delhi, one of the two merging entities
articles.nri_angle: NRIs invested in Indian infrastructure through equity, mutual funds, or bonds will see a reshaped landscape as the merged entity's scale could improve credit ratings and lower borrowing costs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Judge Handling Adani's Case Just Told Prosecutors Their Explanation Wasn't Good Enough
articles.excerpt: Judge Nicholas Garaufis refused to dismiss criminal charges against Gautam Adani outright, ordering the Justice Department to justify dropping the case by July 13.
articles.image_caption: Gautam Adani, founder and chairman of the Adani Group
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with exposure to Indian markets through holdings, index funds, or infrastructure bonds are directly affected by the legal cloud over one of India's largest conglomerates.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gulf Ceasefire Unravels as Iran Fires Missiles at Kuwait and Bahrain. India’s Seafarers Pay the Price.
articles.excerpt: Three Indian sailors are dead, 20,000 seafarers remain stranded in the Persian Gulf, and the fragile US-Iran deal is falling apart — leaving New Delhi caught between its closest strategic partner and its citizens’ safety.
articles.image_caption: Satellite view of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman that has become the epicenter of the US-Iran conflict.
articles.image_credit: NASA/MODIS, Public Domain, via Wikimedia Commons
articles.nri_angle: India's 9 million Gulf workers face direct risk from the escalation. Three Indian seafarers died on the MT Settebello, prompting India to summon the US envoy. Thousands more remain stranded on ships in the Gulf. India's oil imports and domestic inflation are directly tied to Hormuz stability.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Amazon Just Raised Its India Bet to $48 Billion. The Quick Commerce War It Triggered Is Already Drawing Blood.
articles.excerpt: Andy Jassy's visit to New Delhi came with $13 billion in fresh AI and cloud commitments — and a 300-city quick commerce expansion that has wiped $15 billion off Blinkit and Swiggy's market value.
articles.image_caption: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy meets Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi to discuss the company's expanded India investment
articles.nri_angle: NRIs invested in Indian quick commerce stocks face margin compression, while the $80B+ hyperscaler buildout creates high-paying AI jobs and transforms the Indian startup ecosystem
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America's New Ambassador to India Says the Visa Crackdown Isn't About India. Here's What He's Not Saying.
articles.excerpt: Sergio Gor insists H-1B reforms are part of a 'broader overhaul,' not targeted at Indians. But a new wage-based selection system could shut out the entry-level workers who built Silicon Valley's outsourcing pipeline.
articles.image_caption: U.S. Ambassador to India Sergio Gor at the White House
articles.nri_angle: Indians are 72% of H-1B recipients and dominate the green card backlog — the shift to wage-based selection could reshape the pathway that brought millions of Indian professionals to America
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Hyderabad Names Road 'Donald Trump Avenue' in First Such Honour for a US President in India
articles.excerpt: Telangana's Congress government renamed a road near the US Consulate and tech offices of Microsoft, Google, and Amazon as part of a broader initiative to position Hyderabad as a global innovation hub — drawing both praise from Trump and sharp political backlash at home.
articles.image_caption: US President Donald Trump thanked India for the road naming honour in Hyderabad, calling it a historic first for a US president.
articles.image_credit: White House official portrait, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
articles.nri_angle: Hyderabad's Financial District hosts the India offices of Microsoft, Google, Amazon, and many other American tech firms, making it a key nexus for the Indian-American tech workforce. The road naming amid ongoing trade negotiations signals deepening US-India economic ties that directly affect NRI professionals and investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Launches Aarogya Setu 2.0, Unveils Sweeping Digital Health Overhaul
articles.excerpt: Health Minister JP Nadda rolled out nearly a dozen interconnected platforms — from AI-powered health records and wearable integration to a WhatsApp chatbot and a unified drug registry — in India's most ambitious push yet to digitise healthcare for 1.4 billion people.
articles.image_caption: Union Health Minister JP Nadda launched Aarogya Setu 2.0 and a suite of digital health initiatives on June 29, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: The ABHA system lets NRIs access family health records remotely, wearable integration connects parents' fitness trackers to a centralised record, the UHI enables cross-border telemedicine, and Scan & Register/Pay simplifies hospital visits for diaspora members visiting India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pakistan Just Bombed Afghanistan for the Second Time This Month. India Told Islamabad to Stop Blaming Everyone Else.
articles.excerpt: After a Karachi Rangers attack killed three soldiers, Pakistan struck militant hideouts across three Afghan provinces. Kabul says the bombs hit civilians. India called Pakistan’s attempt to link it to the Karachi assault ‘baseless.’
articles.image_caption: Sindh Rangers paramilitary personnel in Pakistan
articles.nri_angle: Nine million Indians work in Gulf states near the conflict zone; a Pakistan-Afghanistan escalation could disrupt migration corridors, energy supply, and regional counterterrorism cooperation that protects diaspora communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Biggest Trade Deal Ever Takes Effect in 16 Days. Here's What Changes for the Diaspora.
articles.excerpt: The India-UK Free Trade Agreement launches July 15 with steep tariff cuts, extended pension portability for professionals, and a steel dispute that almost sank it.
articles.image_caption: India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and UK Trade Secretary Jonathan Reynolds at the India-UK FTA signing ceremony
articles.nri_angle: The FTA includes extended pension portability for professionals moving between India and the UK, directly affecting 1.6 million people of Indian origin in Britain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Reopened All Three Himalayan Trade Routes With China. The Last Caravan Crossed Seven Years Ago.
articles.excerpt: Lipulekh, Shipki La, and Nathu La are all active again for the first time since the Galwan clash. Traders no longer need mules. The Kailash Mansarovar Yatra is back. And for the first time ever, transactions will be in rupees and yuan, not barter.
articles.image_caption: The road to Nathu La Pass in Sikkim, one of three Himalayan trade corridors reopened on the India-China border
articles.nri_angle: The Kailash Mansarovar Yatra’s return restores access to one of the most sacred pilgrimage sites for millions of Hindus, Jains, and Buddhists in the diaspora, while the trade reopening signals an India-China normalisation that could reshape investment and travel calculus for NRIs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kotak Mahindra's CEO Is Leaving After Less Than Three Years. The Bank Has Now Lost Two Leaders Since Its Founder Stepped Down.
articles.excerpt: Ashok Vaswani, a Barclays and Citigroup veteran who was handpicked to succeed billionaire Uday Kotak, told the board he will not seek reappointment. The stock fell 3.3 percent.
articles.image_caption: Kotak Mahindra Bank, India's fourth-largest private sector lender
articles.nri_angle: Kotak Mahindra Bank serves millions of NRI customers through NRE/NRO accounts, remittances, and digital banking — a leadership vacuum at the top affects the diaspora's banking experience directly.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Indian-Born Billionaire in Canada Just Parked $1 Billion in Indian Bonds. It's Not About the Bonds.
articles.excerpt: Prem Watsa's Fairfax bought nearly $1 billion in Indian government debt in a single week — positioning to acquire a majority stake in state-owned IDBI Bank in what could be India's biggest bank privatisation ever.
articles.image_caption: Prem Watsa, the Indian-Canadian billionaire who chairs Fairfax Financial Holdings
articles.nri_angle: If Prem Watsa's Fairfax wins IDBI Bank, it would be the first time a foreign-origin investor takes control of a major Indian bank — reshaping NRI banking, remittances, and India's privatisation programme.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: They Donated From Abroad to Build the Ram Temple. Eight Men Were Stealing the Money.
articles.excerpt: A court in Ayodhya has detained eight men — including banking staff — over the systematic embezzlement of devotee donations at India's most politically charged temple. The racket ran for years.
articles.image_caption: The Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, consecrated by Prime Minister Modi in January 2024
articles.nri_angle: NRIs across the US, UK, Canada, and Gulf donated heavily to the Ram Mandir trust — the embezzlement scandal raises urgent questions about financial governance and accountability for diaspora donors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Harmanpreet Hit Three Sixes in One Over at Lord's. India's Women Still Went Home.
articles.excerpt: India posted their highest-ever T20 World Cup score against Australia — and it wasn't enough. Perry and Gardner's century stand knocked India out at the group stage.
articles.image_caption: India captain Harmanpreet Kaur scored a blistering 56 off 27 balls at Lord's
articles.nri_angle: British Indians packed Lord's to cheer the women's team, and NRIs worldwide followed the tournament — India's group-stage exit, coming hours after the men's Ireland debacle, was a painful double blow.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Supreme Court Just Saved the Fed From Trump. Here's Why India Should Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: A 5-4 ruling preserving the Federal Reserve's independence has direct implications for the rupee, NRI remittances, and the institutional trust that underpins Indian-American wealth.
articles.image_caption: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, whose firing by President Trump was blocked by the Supreme Court
articles.nri_angle: Nearly five million Indian-Americans hold US investments and rely on Fed-driven rate decisions — a politicised central bank would introduce sovereign risk to their portfolios and shake the $125 billion remittance corridor.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Central Bank Just Gave NRIs a Reason to Move Their Dollars Home. Banks Are in a Frenzy to Cash In.
articles.excerpt: The RBI is bearing the hedging cost on foreign currency deposits so NRIs can earn 7% risk-free on their dollars. Banks are scrambling to attract up to $100 billion, and the diaspora holds the key to rescuing the rupee.
articles.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
articles.nri_angle: NRIs can earn 6-7% risk-free on dollar deposits as India's central bank absorbs currency hedging costs — a rare moment when the diaspora's savings are being actively courted to rescue the rupee.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He Made Ireland Beat India Twice in Three Days. Then He Quit.
articles.excerpt: Heinrich Malan is stepping down as Ireland's head coach on the back of cricket's biggest upset of the year. Gary Wilson becomes the first Irish-born coach in over 30 years. India, meanwhile, is in 'disbelief.'
articles.image_caption: The Ireland cricket team
articles.nri_angle: India's cricket humiliation in Belfast resonates deeply with the diaspora — many followed the IPL from abroad and now face ribbing from Irish and British colleagues as the team heads to England next.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Launched Two Anti-Dumping Probes in One Week. One Could Make Its Own Power Grid More Expensive.
articles.excerpt: New Delhi is cracking down on cheap steel from China, Japan, and Russia — but duties on transformer-grade electrical steel could slow a ₹9 lakh crore grid expansion that India can't afford to delay.
articles.image_caption: A stainless steel production plant
articles.nri_angle: India's ₹9 lakh crore power grid expansion — which NRI investors have poured into through infrastructure bonds and mutual funds — could face higher costs if anti-dumping duties raise transformer steel prices, while the trade crackdown on Chinese steel signals shifting investment dynamics in India's manufacturing sector.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Signed a Trade Deal With Europe. Now It's Begging Brussels Not to Cut Off Its Metal Scrap.
articles.excerpt: The EU's planned scrap export ban could tighten steel and aluminium supply for India's manufacturers — and undermine a trade agreement that isn't even in force yet.
articles.image_caption: Aluminium swarf at a recycling facility in Germany
articles.nri_angle: NRIs in European manufacturing, recycling, and commodity trading face direct exposure to the scrap policy shift, while the India-EU trade deal's success — and the investment climate it creates — matters to diaspora professionals and businesses on both sides.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Pune IT Firm Just Made One of India's Biggest-Ever Overseas Tech Acquisitions. The Company It Bought Was Founded by Indians in Germany.
articles.excerpt: Persistent Systems is paying $1.3 billion for Nagarro SE, creating a $2.9 billion AI-led engineering giant with 46,000 employees. The stock dropped 11% on the news.
articles.image_caption: The skyline of western Pune, home to Persistent Systems' headquarters and India's growing IT corridor
articles.nri_angle: The deal creates cross-border career pathways between India and Europe for tech workers, and is a landmark moment for Indian IT's shift from back-office outsourcing to AI-led global leadership.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rubio Says Washington Is Planning a Trump Visit to India Early Next Year. He'll Fly Out First to Set It Up.
articles.excerpt: The Secretary of State told Indian media the US is 'on the last inches' of a trade deal and expects to visit New Delhi himself before year-end — but the relationship has a year's worth of bruises to show for the delay.
articles.image_caption: President Donald Trump meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a bilateral summit
articles.nri_angle: A presidential visit and the trade deal in its 'last inches' directly affect visa processing, consular cooperation, and the bilateral mood that shapes life for 4.4 million Indian Americans.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jio Is Filing for India's Biggest IPO Ever. None of Its Major Investors Plan to Sell.
articles.excerpt: Reliance's telecom-to-AI arm is pitching a valuation of up to $170 billion. Meta, Google and KKR are staying in. Every rupee raised goes straight into the company — and India's second half is about to absorb more than $15 billion in new listings.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, India's oldest stock exchange
articles.nri_angle: Jio's listing could be the first Indian mega-IPO large enough to actively court NRI capital, amid a broader RBI push to draw diaspora money into Indian financial instruments.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Just Fined an Indian-Origin Attorney $255,000 for Filing Fake Asylum Claims. It Has Never Done That Before.
articles.excerpt: DHS says California-based Vinod Doddamani submitted 64 nearly identical asylum declarations on behalf of Indian nationals — and the penalty signals a much broader crackdown.
articles.image_caption: The Nebraska Avenue Complex, headquarters of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, in Washington, D.C.
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals are disproportionately named in recent US asylum fraud cases, raising scrutiny on the entire community and potentially affecting legitimate asylum seekers fleeing persecution.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi's Biggest Cabinet Shake-Up in a Decade Could Replace His Finance and Education Ministers This Week
articles.excerpt: Nirmala Sitharaman may lose the finance portfolio she has held for seven years, Dharmendra Pradhan faces removal over the NEET crisis, and the reshuffle is being designed for 2027 state elections.
articles.image_caption: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman during a bilateral meeting in Vienna, April 2025
articles.nri_angle: A change at the finance ministry directly affects NRI deposit schemes, FCNR rates, capital gains exemptions, and FDI policy — every major financial decision for the diaspora runs through this portfolio.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Washington Is Quietly Dismantling Every Path Indians Used to Stay in America
articles.excerpt: Green card rules rewritten, student visas capped, Day 1 CPT under siege. 30,000 Indian students have already left. Germany and the UK are picking up the pieces.
articles.image_caption: The US Capitol building at dusk in Washington, DC, where immigration policy is being reshaped
articles.nri_angle: These policy changes affect virtually every Indian professional and student in the United States — from green card applicants in the 100-year backlog to families who mortgaged homes to send children to American universities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran and the US Agreed to Stand Down. India's 9 Million Gulf Workers — and Its Oil Lifeline — Are Watching.
articles.excerpt: A weekend of missiles and air-raid sirens in Kuwait and Bahrain gives way to a fragile promise to resume talks in Qatar on Tuesday
articles.image_caption: Satellite view of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway between Iran and Oman through which a fifth of the world's oil once passed daily
articles.nri_angle: Nine million Indians across the Gulf woke to air-raid sirens again this weekend — the ceasefire's fate directly determines their safety, their remittances, and India's economic stability.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Canada's $500 Billion Defence Spending Surge Just Opened the Door to India. Here's What's Actually on the Table.
articles.excerpt: High Commissioner Christopher Cooter describes a 'hockey stick' trajectory in military spending and a 'transformative' partnership after years of diplomatic freeze
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi meets Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, whose election reset a relationship frozen by the Khalistan dispute
articles.nri_angle: For 1.8 million Indian-Canadians, the defence rapprochement signals a stabilisation of bilateral ties that had chilled visa processing and people-to-people exchanges.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Flew a Field Hospital Halfway Around the World to Help Venezuela Dig Out
articles.excerpt: Operation Amistad sent two C-17s loaded with surgeons, portable ICUs and India's indigenous BHISHM cubes on a 14,300-km airlift — one of New Delhi's longest humanitarian missions ever.
articles.image_caption: Indian Air Force C-17 Globemaster III transport aircraft
articles.nri_angle: India's growing global humanitarian reach — from disaster relief in Türkiye to Venezuela — signals a foreign-policy posture the diaspora can point to as evidence of a country punching above its weight.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Built Its First Military Aircraft. A Private Company Did It Months Ahead of Schedule.
articles.excerpt: The Tata-Airbus C-295 completed its maiden flight from Vadodara on June 10, making it the first military aircraft ever manufactured in India by a private-sector company — with 85% of the structure built by Indian MSMEs.
articles.image_caption: First India-built C-295 transport aircraft during its maiden flight from Vadodara, Gujarat, on June 10, 2026
articles.nri_angle: For decades, India's tag as the world's largest arms importer embarrassed the diaspora. The C-295 assembly line signals a real shift — a private Indian company building military aircraft to global standards, with an ecosystem of MSMEs riding along.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Signed 19 Agreements in Seychelles Today. Here's What India Got — and What It Gave.
articles.excerpt: A warship, UPI for the island nation, an extradition treaty, a space cooperation pact, 500 tonnes of rice, and a plan to build a national hospital — all in one afternoon on a 115-island archipelago.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi during bilateral talks with Seychelles President Patrick Herminie in Victoria, June 2026
articles.nri_angle: India exporting UPI to Seychelles means the diaspora's digital payment stack is becoming the Indian Ocean's default — and the strategic footprint in a region where China is spending aggressively sends a message NRIs in the Gulf and East Africa understand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI Just Hired the Man Who Ran Uber India to Lead Its Biggest Bet Outside America
articles.excerpt: Prabhjeet Singh will become OpenAI's most senior leader in India, a market with 100 million weekly ChatGPT users and growing faster than any other outside the US.
articles.image_caption: Wikimedia Commons image: File:OpenAI brain network visualization.png
articles.nri_angle: IIT Kharagpur and IIM Ahmedabad alumnus leads OpenAI in India, joining a lineage of Indian-origin leaders at global tech giants — and India is now OpenAI's second-largest market after the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The US Banned Its Most Powerful AI From Leaving the Country. India Decided It Was Time to Build Its Own.
articles.excerpt: After the Anthropic export ban exposed India's dependency on American AI, Delhi sent its IT secretary to Washington, partially won back access — and quietly accelerated a sovereign model that already speaks 22 languages.
articles.image_caption: Server racks at a high-performance computing data center
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin tech workers who build frontier AI models at US companies now face the question of whether those tools will stay accessible to India — the Anthropic ban made that risk real.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Is Negotiating to Sell Its Fastest Missile to the UAE. The Iran War Made It Possible.
articles.excerpt: Talks to export BrahMos and the Akashteer air-defence system mark India's biggest defence pitch to the Gulf — and a direct counter to Pakistan's deepening ties with Saudi Arabia.
articles.image_caption: A BrahMos supersonic cruise missile launcher on display during India's Republic Day parade in New Delhi
articles.nri_angle: 3.4 million Indians in the UAE stand to benefit from a deeper defence relationship that strengthens bilateral ties and India's strategic standing in the Gulf.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and the US Say a Trade Deal Is Days Away. Here's What's Actually Holding It Up.
articles.excerpt: Greer flew to Delhi, Goyal flew to London, and both sides called it 'very, very close.' But the Supreme Court ruling, Section 301, and a July 24 deadline are making the final stretch harder than the first mile.
articles.image_caption: India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who has led trade negotiations with the United States
articles.nri_angle: A trade deal would lower tariffs on Indian goods in the U.S. and ease diplomatic tensions affecting visa policy and the business environment for Indian-American entrepreneurs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NASA's Chief Just Offered to Help India Build Its Own Space Station. India Hasn't Said Yes.
articles.excerpt: Bill Nelson's India visit confirms an ISRO astronaut will fly to the ISS by 2027. The bigger question is whether New Delhi wants American help on the station it plans to build by 2035.
articles.image_caption: NASA astronaut Raja Chari with ISRO officials at Johnson Space Center, reflecting deepening US-India space ties
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American scientists and engineers at NASA have shaped US space exploration for decades; a deeper ISRO-NASA partnership creates new opportunities for Indian space startups and strengthens the technology bridge between both countries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Europe's Worst Heatwave on Record Has Killed Over 1,000 in France. Two Million Indians Live in Its Path.
articles.excerpt: Scientists say the 40°C-plus temperatures shattering records from Germany to Britain would have been 'virtually impossible' without climate change. The same forces are weakening India's monsoon.
articles.image_caption: Satellite thermal image showing hot surface temperatures across Europe during the record-breaking June 2026 heatwave
articles.nri_angle: Over two million people of Indian origin live across Europe, concentrated in the UK, Germany, and France — the countries hardest hit by the heatwave. The same climate forces weakening India's monsoon are driving Europe's deadly heat.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
